subject: POC prompt dataset collection & evaluation plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Lee <jason.lee@acmecorp.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: POC prompt dataset collection & evaluation plan

Hi Jason / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today — really appreciated the clear run‑through of your primary flows and the goals for the POC. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

1) Success criteria (please confirm):
   - Generation accuracy: 85%+ on domain QA prompts (as judged by your SMEs)
   - Latency: 95th percentile < 400ms for single-turn queries
   - Cost: target average token cost < $0.004 / token (we'll show model/quantization tradeoffs)

2) Evaluation plan and dataset:
   - For the POC we'll need a representative prompt set + any recent logs you can share (sample of 500–2,000 prompts).
   - Preferred format: CSV with columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_output (if available), metadata (flow, channel).
   - If you have full request/response logs, a zipped export is fine — we'll only use them to build eval sets; we can sign an NDA/limited-use clause if needed.

3) Timeline / ownership:
   - You provide dataset and success criteria: by EOD Thu 8/27
   - Redwood ingests dataset & proposes prompt/eval split: 8/28–8/30
   - POC run & results: 9/1–9/10
   - Checkpoint call to review results: week of 9/13

Action items for Acme: share the prompt CSV (or logs) and call out any labels/SME reviewers.

Attachments: example CSV template attached.

Thanks — I’ll loop Rishi/Dev on infra/throughput items after we have the dataset.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[attachment: prompts-template.csv (text/csv, 2KB)]

From: Jason Lee <jason.lee@acmecorp.com>

Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: Re: POC prompt dataset collection & evaluation plan

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap — that matches our expectations. We generated the sample exports from our production logs (redacted PII) and attached two files: a CSV of 1,200 prompts and a zipped archive of the raw request/response logs for Aug 2026. Notes:

- prompts-acme-20260824.csv: includes columns prompt_id, prompt_text, channel, expected_output (where available). We flagged ~200 examples with gold annotations.
- acme-logs-20260824.zip: contains full request/response payloads. Password: Acme2026! (we'll share SFTP if that doesn't work).

A couple clarifying points:
- For expected_output we're focusing on content fidelity (is the answer correct/guiding the user), not perfect wording.
- We can provide SME reviewers (Priya + 2 others) for the 200 gold examples for evaluation.
- On latency: our live traffic has 95p ~ 320ms so your target looks good.

Let us know if you need the files in another schema.

Attachments: [attachment: prompts-acme-20260824.csv (text/csv, 180KB)], [attachment: acme-logs-20260824.zip (application/zip, 12.3MB)]

—Jason

Thanks — saw the uploads. Small ops notes: 

- We'll ingest the CSV and run an initial dedup/normalization pass (remove identical prompts and standardize channel tags).
- For logs, we'll extract the request/response pairs and bucket by length/flow for throughput profiling.
- Suggest we provision a short Dedicated trial node (g5-style equivalent) for the POC so we can hit real latency numbers; Marissa, can you confirm if Acme is open to trialing Dedicated for the 2‑week run?

I'll own the ingestion and perf profiling. Marissa, I'll work with Dev to get the Dedicated pool staged if Acme agrees.
